map.An integers & coordinate-plane adventure: A story about integers & the coordinate plane, in five chapters. It has six reader gates. Solve the math to relight the city.
map.Pattern distortion: severe. City power:: The patterns are very bent. City power: failing. Reader: bundle up.
map.Previously, in Volume Six: the crew forg: Last time, in Volume Six: the crew made the master key. They opened Ada Vex's cipher vault and stopped the glitch that scrambled the city's signs. The vault's last page said: "When the lights go out, start at zero." Tonight, in midwinter, the lights went out.
map.Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engi: Fact one: Ada Vex built the Pattern Engine where Meridian Avenue crosses Zero Street. Right in the middle.
map.Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. T: Her street grid IS a coordinate plane. The engine sits at the origin, (0, 0). Power spreads out from zero, district by district.
map.East–west streets count along the x-axis: East–west streets count along the x-axis. North–south streets count along the y-axis. They cross at the origin.
map.Below-zero numbers. Whole ones with no f: Below-zero numbers. Whole ones with no fraction attached: integers, right?
map.Correct. Integers: counting numbers, the: Correct. Integers: counting numbers, their opposites, and zero. Opposites sit the same distance from zero, on the other side. The heat router wakes when its dial shows the opposite of tonight's reading, −7.
map.The heat router needs yesterday's log. P: The heat router needs yesterday's log. Pick a reading chip, then tap its tick on the thermometer: −8°, −3°, and 5°. Then wake the router. Its dial must show the opposite of −7. Type that number.
map.Conceptual: zero is the freezing mark. N: Conceptual: zero is the freezing mark. Negative readings are BELOW zero. The deeper the negative, the LOWER the tick. Opposites sit the same distance from zero, on the other side.
map.Procedural: start at 0 and count ticks D: Procedural: start at 0 and count ticks DOWN for a negative reading: −3 is three ticks below zero. For an opposite, keep the distance from zero and switch sides.
map.Heater trucks roll to the coldest distri: Heater trucks go to the coldest district first. But which IS coldest? One reading is a fraction.
map.Don't trust your eyes. Under a minus sig: Don't trust your eyes. After a minus sign, a big digit means a deep freeze.
map.All four are rational numbers — any numb: All four are rational numbers: any number you can write as a fraction, like −2.5 or −¾. Different costumes, same number line.
map.Rational numbers include integers, fract: Rational numbers include integers, fractions, and decimals, positive and negative. Least means farthest below zero.
map.Sort the ledger, reader — the coldest di: Sort the list, reader. The coldest district gets the first truck!
map.Four district readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°: Four district readings: −2.5°, 0.5°, −3°, −¾°. Tap the cards in order from least to greatest (coldest district first). Tap a card again to take it back.
map.Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW z: Conceptual: colder means farther BELOW zero. On a number line the least number is farthest left. With negatives, a bigger-looking digit means a colder reading.
map.Procedural: rewrite everything the same: Procedural: write everything the same way first. As a decimal, three fourths is 0.75, so −¾ = −0.75. Then slide along the number line from left to right.
map.Distance, not direction. The bars in |−6: Distance, not direction. The bars in |−6| mean absolute value: how far from zero, ignoring the sign.
map.Absolute value is never negative. Direct: Absolute value is never negative. A sign shows direction. The bars show distance.
map.Set the booster strengths, reader. Then: Set the booster strengths, reader. Then say which station is farther out.
map.Booster strength = the station's absolut: Booster strength = the station's absolute value (its distance from the engine at zero). Set both: |−6| for Station W and |4| for Station E. Then say which station is farther from zero.
map.Conceptual: absolute value bars measure: Conceptual: absolute value bars measure DISTANCE from zero. Distance has no sign: |−9| and |9| are both 9.
map.Procedural: count steps from 0 to the st: Procedural: count steps from 0 to the station on the number line. For 'farther from zero,' compare the two distances. Pick the station with the bigger distance.
map.Ada's map cuts the city into four quadra: Ada's map cuts the city into four quadrants. They go counterclockwise from the upper right: I, II, III, IV.
map.Every station is an ordered pair (x, y):: Every station is an ordered pair (x, y): blocks east–west first, then north–south. (2, 5) is NOT (5, 2).
map.Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and: Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and (4, −1). But the blackout scrambled my map. Five dots flicker, and only two are real.
map.An ordered pair (x, y) locates a point:: An ordered pair (x, y) tells where a point is: x first (left–right), then y (up–down).
map.Read the pairs carefully, reader. Light: Read the pairs carefully, reader. If you light the wrong relay, we waste the power we have.
map.Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). T: Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). The first number moves you left (negative) or right (positive) from the origin. The second moves you down (negative) or up (positive).
map.Procedural: walk each pair: for (−1, 4): Procedural: walk each pair. For (−1, 4) you go 1 block left, then 4 blocks up. Quadrants count counterclockwise from the upper right: I, then II, then III, then IV.
map.Cable time. Even elevation runs below ze: Cable time. Even heights go below zero down here: the old platform sits at −6 meters.
map.Measure both cable runs in blocks. Cable: Measure both cable runs in blocks. Cable A: (−3, 4) to (5, 4). Cable B: (2, −1) to (2, −6). Count exactly. Priya cuts only once.
map.Conceptual: when two points share a coor: Conceptual: when two points share a coordinate, the cable runs straight. If the numbers that change are on OPPOSITE sides of zero, ADD their absolute values. On the same side of zero? SUBTRACT them.
map.Procedural: like (−4, 1) to (2, 1): x cr: Procedural: for (−4, 1) to (2, 1), x crosses zero, so |−4| + |2| = 6 blocks. For (7, −2) to (7, −9), same side, so 9 − 2 = 7 blocks.
map.Boss Gate: distances on the plane, plus: Boss Gate: distances on the plane, and the perimeter of a polygon drawn on the grid.
map.Conceptual: a side's length is the dista: Conceptual: a side's length is the distance between the coordinates that CHANGE. If they are on opposite sides of zero, add the two distances. The perimeter is the whole trip around all four sides.
map.Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6: Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6 crosses zero: 2 + 6 = 8 blocks. Perimeter shortcut: 2 × (width + height).
map.Achievement unlocked: city un-frozen. Ho: Achievement unlocked: city un-frozen. The hot cocoa race starts now.
map.New distortion below city hall. A door s: A new bent pattern below city hall. A door shaped like a balance scale. It wants things EQUAL. To be continued...
map.Crew co-captain. Keeps the notebook, ask: Crew co-captain. Keeps the notebook and asks the next question. This volume: called the quadrant order that relit the city.
map.Evidence officer and co-lead. This volum: Evidence officer and co-lead. This volume: turned a frozen thermometer into an integer lesson.
map.Builder and cable boss. This volume: mea: Builder and cable boss. This volume: measured every run with absolute values, and cut once.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Senses bent patterns but cannot compute. That's your job.
map.Rational numbers.Any number you can writ: Rational numbers.Any number you can write as a fraction: −3, −2.5, −¾, 0.5. They all share one number line. Least sits farthest left.
map.Ordered pairs & quadrants.(x, y): x move: Ordered pairs & quadrants.(x, y): x moves left–right, y moves up–down. The axes cut the plane into quadrants I–IV, counterclockwise from the upper right.
map.Distance on the plane.Points sharing a c: Distance on the plane.Points that share a coordinate make a straight path. Opposite sides of zero → add absolute values. Same side → subtract.
map.completed Volume 7: Below Zero and prove: completed Volume 7: Below Zero and showed skill with integers, opposites, rational numbers, absolute value, the four quadrants, and distance on the coordinate plane.
map.Its opposite keeps the same distance — s: Its opposite keeps the same distance, six, but switches sides: six ticks UP lands on 6.
Rewrite as decimals: −1.5, 1, −0.5, −2. The deepest below zero is −2. That's the least.
map.Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negati: Left to right: −2, −1.5, −0.5, 1. Negatives can fool you. Always check the distance below zero.
map.8 > 3, so the station at −8 is farther f: 8 > 3, so the station at −8 is farther from zero, even though −8 is the SMALLER number.
map.Left and down lands in Quadrant III — th: Left and down lands in Quadrant III. That's where both signs are negative.
map.Measure (−6, 3) to (3, 3): the y-values: Measure (−6, 3) to (3, 3): the y-values match, so the run goes sideways.
map.x goes from −6 to 3 — opposite sides of: x goes from −6 to 3. These are opposite sides of zero, so add the distances: |−6| + |3| = 9 blocks.
map.Now (4, −1) to (4, −7): both y-values ar: Now (4, −1) to (4, −7): both y-values are below zero, on the same side, so subtract: 7 − 1 = 6 blocks.
map.Place all three readings on the thermome: Place all three readings on the thermometer first. Tap a chip, then a tick.
map.A negative reading lives BELOW the zero: A negative reading is BELOW the zero mark. Check which side of 0 your tick is on.
map.−8 is COLDER than −3 — deeper below zero: −8 is COLDER than −3. Deeper below zero means a LOWER tick.
map.At least one reading sits on the wrong t: At least one reading is on the wrong tick. Count ticks from 0 carefully.
map.Readings logged, dial at 7 — the heat ro: Readings logged, dial at 7. The heat router hums awake!
map.Readings placed! Now the dial: an opposi: Readings placed! Now the dial: an opposite keeps the distance from zero but switches sides.
−3 < −2.5 < −¾ < 0.5. Frostvale first. Heater trucks roll out, coldest district leading!
map.Careful — −¾ is only ¾ below zero. −2.5: Careful: −¾ is only ¾ below zero. −2.5 is two and a half below. Colder sinks lower.
map.Not coldest-to-warmest yet. Picture all: Not coldest-to-warmest yet. Picture all four on a number line before you tap.
map.Distance is never negative — drop the si: Distance is never negative. Drop the sign inside the bars.
map.Absolute value asks: how many steps from: Absolute value asks: how many steps from 0? Count them on the line.
map.Strengths are set… now compare the two d: Strengths are set. Now compare the two distances you found. Which one is bigger?
map.Boosters set: 6 and 4. Station W at −6 s: Boosters set: 6 and 4. Station W at −6 is farther from zero, so it gets the big booster. Signal restored!
map.Check the signs: in (−3, 2), the −3 mean: Check the signs: in (−3, 2), the −3 means 3 blocks LEFT of the engine, not right.
map.The second number is the up–down move: (: The second number is the up–down move: (−3, 2) goes UP 2. It doesn't go down.
map.Re-walk each pair from the origin: left–: Walk each pair again from the origin: left–right first, then up–down.
map.Relays lit! Now the quadrants — count co: Relays lit! Now the quadrants. Count counterclockwise from the upper right: I, II, III, IV.
map.(−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II and (4, −1): (−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II and (4, −1) in Quadrant IV. The relays link across the city!
map.Cable A crosses x = 0 — don't subtract s: Cable A crosses x = 0, so don't subtract straight across zero. Add each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Cable A runs sideways: only the x-number: Cable A runs sideways: only the x-numbers change. Count the blocks between them.
map.Both y-values sit on the SAME side of ze: Both y-values are on the SAME side of zero. Subtract the smaller distance from the bigger one.
map.Cable B runs up–down: only the y-numbers: Cable B runs up–down: only the y-numbers change. Count carefully below zero.
map.8 blocks across, 5 blocks down — both ca: 8 blocks across, 5 blocks down. Both cables measured with zero slack!
map.Lock 1 holds. Width: x runs from −4 to 3: Lock 1 holds. Width: x runs from −4 to 3, opposite sides of zero, so ADD each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Lock 2 holds. Height: y runs from −2 up: Lock 2 holds. Height: y runs from −2 up to 3, opposite sides again. Add the distances.
map.Lock 3 holds. 35 is the AREA inside the: Lock 3 holds. 35 is the AREA inside the ring. The cable runs around the EDGE. Add all four sides.
map.Lock 3 holds. That's one width plus one: Lock 3 holds. That's one width plus one height. The ring needs BOTH widths and BOTH heights.
map.Lock 3 holds. Perimeter is the whole tri: Lock 3 holds. Perimeter is the whole trip around: width + height + width + height.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close the ring. The Light Ring blazes and Axiom City relights, quadrant by quadrant!
map.Walk the steps above again — you've got: Go back over the steps above. You can do this.
